steps.tx: **Pyridoxal phosphate**, PLP, is the active form of vitamin B6. It grips amino acids at enzyme active sites, so it serves nearly every amino acid transformation. Transaminases are the famous examples, but the full list matters more: decarboxylases, cystathionine synthase and the first enzyme of haem synthesis all depend on the same coenzyme.
steps.say: PLP is the amino acid coenzyme. Wherever amino groups move, carbon skeletons rearrange or haem begins, pyridoxal phosphate is usually holding the substrate.

steps.tx: **Decarboxylase products** explain the neurology. PLP dependent decarboxylases make GABA, histamine, dopamine and serotonin precursors. ALA synthase, also PLP dependent, is the rate limiting first step of haem synthesis and the most commonly forgotten entry. Glycogen phosphorylase holds most body PLP by bulk, a favourite factual aside in examinations.
steps.say: GABA, histamine and dopamine all come from PLP decarboxylases. Add ALA synthase starting haem synthesis, plus phosphorylase storing most PLP, and the list is complete.

steps.tx: **Deficiency signs** reflect those enzymes failing. Sideroblastic anaemia appears when ALA synthase cannot start haem production, leaving iron loaded mitochondria ringed around red cell nuclei. Cheilosis and glossitis mimic riboflavin lack. Infants develop convulsions because GABA synthesis falls, and these seizures respond to pyridoxine when standard drugs fail.
steps.say: Too little B6 gives sideroblastic anaemia, a sore mouth and, in infants, convulsions from low GABA. Pyridoxine dependent seizures are the dramatic, treatable version.

steps.tx: **Isoniazid inactivation** is the classic drug interaction. Isoniazid binds and inactivates pyridoxine, so tuberculosis therapy can cause peripheral neuropathy and seizures. Pyridoxine is therefore co-prescribed, especially in pregnancy, diabetes, alcohol use disorder and malnutrition. Hydralazine and penicillamine antagonise B6 by similar chemistry and appear as alternative culprits in exam stems.
steps.say: Isoniazid disables pyridoxine, so TB treatment pairs the two in anyone at risk. Hydralazine and penicillamine play the same trick in examination questions.

steps.tx: **Excess neuropathy** is the paradox to state plainly. Chronic megadoses of pyridoxine cause a sensory peripheral neuropathy with numbness and unsteady gait, closely mimicking deficiency. Both too little and far too much B6 injure peripheral nerves, so supplement doses should stay near physiological need unless a specific indication demands more.
steps.say: Here is the paradox examiners love: B6 lack injures nerves, and B6 megadoses injure them too. Sensory neuropathy can mean either extreme.

steps.tx: **Homocystinuria cross reference** ties B6 to sulfur amino acids. Cystathionine synthase needs PLP, so some patients with inherited defects in this enzyme respond to large pyridoxine doses that push residual activity. A PLP responsive homocystinuria improves biochemically and clinically on B6, distinguishing it from forms needing dietary restriction and betaine instead.
steps.say: Some homocystinuria patients respond to high dose B6 because their faulty enzyme still uses PLP. Testing responsiveness is a standard step before strict diets.
